newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine singer Sosa's political bid doubtful.
newsitem.headline: Argentine singer Sosa's political bid doubtful.

text.p: Popular Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa is unlikely, as was speculated, to run for Congress this year on a slate headed by former Radical Party President Raul Alfonsin, local newspapers said on Friday.
"I would be honoured if Mercedes Sosa joined me (in Buenos Aires province), but I don't think she can because she was born in (the northern province of) Tucuman," Alfonsin was quoted.

Sosa, whose deep, powerful vocals and versions of popular folk songs like "Gracias a la vida" (Thanks to Life) have won her a huge following in Latin America and beyond, refused to comment on the media reports.
Clarin and La Nacion newspapers on Thursday predicted Sosa would clinch the third slot on the Radical list which Alfonsin aims to head in October mid-term elections.

The Radicals will vie with centre-left coalition Frepaso for liberal votes in the province, the country's largest electoral district that has traditionally been the stronghold of the ruling Peronist party.
Sosa is an outspoken supporter of Alfonsin, who was elected president in 1983 and who steered Argentina to democracy after six years of military dictatorship.
